## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Limited information is available about the wave sizes this break works in.
- Limited information is available about this break's preferred tide conditions.
- Limited information is available about how this wave breaks.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Six readable sources from four publishers (Wikipedia x2, Surf-Forecast x2, Research, Society and Development, nazarewaves.com). Wind: Surf-Forecast says east (both pages), matching the profile's 90; nazarewaves.com says NE ideally or N, which is 45 deg off (edge of agreement), so the evidence points to E to NE rather than exactly E. Swell direction: W (Surf-Forecast) and NW (nazarewaves) bracket the profile's 280-310 optimum; no source gives degrees. Period: two sources give 14 s or more as the threshold for the canyon effect (profile minimum 13 s, ideal 17 s). They are not independent: the 2022 paper and nazarewaves.com list the same three conditions (14 s or more, over 4 m, about 3x amplification), so one probably drew on the other. The RSD journal is an open-access Brazilian journal with fast review (received 08/06, accepted 08/25/2022); treat it as weak peer review. Size: no source gives a working range in breaking-face feet. The '4 m' threshold is the offshore or forecast wave height for the area, not a face height, so it was not recorded; the 15 m and 24-28 m figures are storm or record waves. Bottom type conflict: Surf-Forecast's Praia do Norte page says reef; its Nazare page and Wikipedia say beach. Tide: only Surf-Forecast (all tides); the profile has no preference. Gaps: no official source. The Instituto Hidrográfico page that nazarewaves.com cites is 404. Crossref searches found no surf-break wave-focusing study of Praia do Norte with a readable abstract other than the RSD paper; the ResearchGate study mentioned in the earlier notes (275-315 deg focusing) was not found.

### Swell period

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ideal | — | not documented | — | `ideal_swell_period_s` 17 s |
| Acceptable | 14 s or more | documented | S4, S5 | `min_swell_period_s` 13 s (minimum) |
| Short-period behaviour | — | not documented | — | no spot-specific setting (periods below `min_swell_period_s` score lower) |
| Long-period behaviour | the canyon focuses extra swell, especially longer-period swell, and can amplify the forecast wave size about three times | documented | S4 | no spot-specific setting |

Notes:

- **Ideal**: The excerpts give a threshold (14 s or more) but no ideal period.
- **Acceptable**: The 2022 RSD paper and nazarewaves.com both say the canyon effect typically needs a wave period of 14 s or more; the two list the same conditions and may not be independent.
  - S4 (Research, Society and Development): “the Nazaré Canyon can amplify 3 times the wave size presented by forecasts to the Nazaré zone - typically, wave period equal to or greater than 14 seconds”
  - S5 (Nazaré Big Waves Surf (nazarewaves.com)): “Wave period equal to or greater than 14 seconds”
- **Short-period behaviour**: No excerpt says what happens below 14 s.
- **Long-period behaviour**: The RSD paper says the canyon head focuses extra swell, especially the longer period, and can amplify the wave size of the Nazare-zone forecasts three times when the period is 14 s or more.
  - S4 (Research, Society and Development): “the headboard is less than 1500 m offshore. What this does is not only focus extra swell (especially the longer period) into the region”
  - S4 (Research, Society and Development): “the Nazaré Canyon can amplify 3 times the wave size presented by forecasts to the Nazaré zone - typically, wave period equal to or greater than 14 seconds”

  - S2 (Wikipedia): “The upper section extends from about 1 km (0.62 mi) off Nazaré to the edge of the continental shelf...Praia do Norte consistently presents waves significantly larger than the rest of the Portuguese”

  - S5 (Nazaré Big Waves Surf (nazarewaves.com)): “the Nazaré Canyon divides the swell into two distinct parts: a swell funneled by the canyon channel and another swell beside the canyon.”
  - S5 (Nazaré Big Waves Surf (nazarewaves.com)): “When these two swells meet again closer to shore, they collide, causing a constructive triangle interaction”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell direction · ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast gives west as the ideal swell direction and nazarewaves.com gives northwest; neither gives degrees.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast pairs the best conditions with an offshore east wind, whereas nazarewaves.com says the ideal wind is from the northeast quadrant, or north.
